title: Empirical Signal Watchdog for Model Rollouts
creator: Marcus Lee
description: Build an experiment-first watchdog service that orchestrates phased model rollouts (canary, A/B, shadow) with automated exposure controls and evidence-based auto-rollback. The watchdog centralizes signal detection, sequential statistical checks, and mitigation actions so product teams can launch model versions with predictable safety envelopes.
objectives: Provide an easy-to-configure experiment manifest for canary/A-B/shadow runs
Enforce per-customer and global exposure caps with gradual ramps
Run continuous sequential statistical tests and surface drift/regression signals
Support automated mitigation: pause, throttle, rollback, and fallback to prior model
Integrate with Console for visibility and operator overrides
success_criteria: New model can be ramped from 0% to target exposure with automated guardrail enforcement
False positive rollback rate < 1% on historical backtests across 50 internal experiments
Detection latency for a 5% QoL regression (primary metric) < 15 minutes at 95% power for medium traffic cohorts
Runbook actions (pause/rollback) available via Console with single-click confirmation
background: We routinely run model variant experiments but lack a unified service that (1) applies exposure policies consistently across customers, (2) performs sequential statistical checks suited to streaming traffic, and (3) triggers safe automated mitigations tied to business-aware metrics. Existing tickets (PM-59012 and PM-47011) tackled traffic-splitting and cohort exposure; this ticket formalizes an empirical signal watchdog that glues statistical checks, policy enforcement, and rollback automation.
proposed_solution: Create a Watchdog microservice that consumes per-request telemetry (tokens, latency, score, quality labels) and experiment manifests. Manifests declare cohorts, primary/secondary metrics, acceptable tolerance bands, alpha spending rules, and mitigation actions. The Watchdog executes continuous sequential tests (alpha-spending O’Brien-Fleming and Bayesian stopping rules), computes per-cohort risk, and enforces exposure caps by updating routing policies in the serving plane (smart routing API). It emits structured alerts to Console and exposes a REST endpoint for operator commands.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): wire Watchdog to internal dev traffic and run shadow experiments for 2 weeks. Phase 2 (beta): support 0.1%–1% external canaries for selected customers with manual override. Phase 3 (GA): fully automated ramping with auto-rollback enabled for non-prod and opt-in for prod customers. Each phase includes backtesting against historical experiment logs and a compliance review. Target GA: 2026-04-01.
metrics: primary_metric: end-user task success rate (binary) - used for sequential tests
secondary_metrics: token-latency P95, hallucination-rate (internal eval proxy), cost-per-inference
exposure_metrics: %requests routed to variant by cohort, per-customer daily exposure
statistical_checks: Sequential A/B test with alpha-spending (O'Brien-Fleming) for primary metric
Bayesian posterior monitoring for small-sample cohorts (report Bayes factor > 10 triggers review)
Non-inferiority margins configurable per metric (default: -1.5% absolute on success rate)
Multiple-hypothesis correction for multi-metric signals using Holm-Bonferroni
Minimum-exposure thresholds and burn-in periods before tests start (e.g., 1k requests or 30 minutes)
exposure_controls: Global ramp schedule (0% → 0.1% → 1% → 5% → target) with hold windows at each step
Per-customer caps (opt-in flag and hard limit; default 2% of a customer’s traffic)
Cohort-based allocation: can define cohorts by org, region, or feature-flag
Shadow mode: duplicate traffic to candidate model without affecting responses
Safety envelopes: auto-throttle when operational metrics exceed thresholds (e.g., P95 latency > 2x baseline)
monitoring_playbook: Console dashboard tab: Watchdog summary, active experiments, per-cohort signals
Alert severity levels: INFO (signal observed), WARNING (metric drift > threshold), CRITICAL (auto-mitigation initiated)
Notification channels: PagerDuty for CRITICAL, Slack channel #watchdog-ops for WARNING
Investigation checklist: reproduce on staging using same sample, inspect token-level traces, check model artifact diff
Escalation: if rollback fails, route traffic to immutable fallback model and open incident with SRE
rollback_policy: Two-tier rollback: (1) soft mitigation: pause ramp and throttle exposure by 50% when a single critical signal fires; (2) hard rollback: revert traffic routing to previous pinned model when multiple critical checks are violated within a 30-minute window. All rollbacks require operator acknowledgement by default; an opt-in automated rollback mode can perform hard rollback automatically when Bayes factor > 50 and primary metric delta exceeds the non-inferiority margin.
risks: Overly aggressive automatic rollbacks causing churn and developer distrust
False negatives for rare but severe failure modes (safety labels not captured by metrics)
Latency introduced by synchronous monitoring calls if not batched
Privacy/regulatory: waveform of per-customer exposure may reveal usage patterns (needs auditing)
mitigations: Conservative default thresholds and two-stage operator confirmation for prod GA
Require custom safety metric hooks for high-risk customers and regulated workloads
Use asynchronous telemetry ingestion and approximate counters to minimize overhead
Audit logs and retention controls; consult legal for regulated countries before enabling auto-rollback
